# Embedded skill: pptx-master

# PPTX Master

Template-first workflow. Every deck starts from `template.pptx` — 49 pre-built on-brand layouts with fonts embedded. Duplicate the layout you need, swap content, save. No building slides from XML.

## Routing (pick one, then read only that section)

| Task | Read section |
|---|---|
| Create a new deck (no .pptx attached) | [Create](#create) |
| Edit / rebrand existing deck (.pptx attached) | [Edit](#edit) |
| QA-only review | [QA](#qa) |
| Brand question only ("what hex is orange?") | [Brand reference](brand-spec.md) — load only when asked |

**Every create or edit run ends with [QA](#qa).** Not optional.

---

## The template

`template.pptx` (sibling of this file) is a 60-slide reference deck. Fonts (Matter, Season Mix) are embedded, so final decks render correctly without font install.

**11 pink slides are section markers — NOT layouts.** Skip: slides 1, 8, 12, 18, 25, 34, 38, 44, 51, 55, 57. Never copy a pink slide into output.

The 49 real layouts are grouped by section:

| Section | Template slides | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| Cover / Title | 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 | Opening slide, hero slide, Q&A transition |
| Agenda / Content intro | 9, 10, 11 | Table of contents, opening statement, pillars |
| Sub dividers | 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 | Section openers inside the deck |
| Product architecture (overview) | 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 | Product roadmap, model lineup, high-level story |
| Product architecture (deep dive) | 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33 | Detailed product/model slides with benchmarks, specs |
| Technical diagrams | 35, 36, 37 | Architecture diagrams, system flows, tech stack |
| Team / Company | 39, 40, 41, 42, 43 | Leadership, partnerships, customer logos |
| Metrics | 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50 | Market stats, growth numbers, comparisons |
| Use cases | 52, 53, 54 | Vertical scenarios, application examples |
| Case study | 56 | Single-case deep dive |
| Thank you / closing | 58, 59, 60 | Closing slide |

**Always browse thumbnails before picking layouts.** Run this once per task:

```bash
mkdir -p thumbs
soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir thumbs template.pptx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 80 thumbs/template.pdf thumbs/t
ls thumbs/t-*.jpg
```

Then `view` the thumbnails for the section you need and pick layouts by slide number.

---

## Create

1. **Browse template thumbnails** (command above). Pick layouts that match the user's outline, by slide number. Ignore pink slides.
2. **Copy template to working file:**
   ```bash
   cp template.pptx deck.pptx
   ```
3. **Delete unused slides** from `deck.pptx`, keeping only the layouts you picked (in the order you want them). Use python-pptx's XML slide manipulation if needed.
4. **Replace text content** in each kept slide. Use python-pptx `paragraph.runs[i].text = "..."` on existing runs to preserve font/size/color styling. Never build new text frames from scratch — reuse the template's.
5. **Swap images** where needed: product screenshots, customer logos, diagrams. Keep shape positions; only replace the image fill.
6. **Run [QA](#qa).**

**Rule:** If a layout's content doesn't fit your message, pick a different layout — don't force text into a slot. If no layout fits, tell the user and ask which section to extend.

---

## Edit

1. **Extract what's there:**
   ```bash
   extract-text /path/to/user-deck.pptx
   ```
2. **Render thumbnails** of the user's deck (same soffice + pdftoppm commands, different input).
3. **For each slide**, decide: keep as-is, fix in place, or replace with a template layout.
   - **Fix in place** when structure is fine but fonts/colors/footer are off. Apply the hard rules below.
   - **Replace** when structure is wrong (e.g. text-only slide, non-brand layout). Copy matching template slide in and port content over.
4. **Apply hard rules (below) to every slide touched.**
5. **Run [QA](#qa).**

---

## QA

Run after every create or edit. Three checks:

**1. Content check** — no placeholder text left:
```bash
extract-text deck.pptx | grep -iE "\bx{3,}\b|lorem|ipsum|\bTODO|\[insert|caption text here|sub divider|cover / title"
```
Any hit = unfixed placeholder. Fix before shipping.

**2. Visual check** — render and inspect:
```bash
soffice --headless --convert-to pdf deck.pptx
rm -f qa-*.jpg
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 deck.pdf qa
ls -1 "$PWD"/qa-*.jpg
```
Then `view` each slide. Look for: text overflow past shape bounds, overlaps, missing footer/monogram on content slides, non-brand fonts (anything that isn't Matter or Season Mix), black backgrounds, `#000000` text.

**3. Hard rules check** — run through the list below. Every violation = fix before shipping.

Stop after one fix-and-verify cycle. Don't chase sub-pixel nudges.

---

## Hard rules (apply to every slide touched)

1. **Fonts:** Season Mix Regular (headings only) or Matter (everything else). No Arial, Calibri, Helvetica. No italics, underlines, strikethrough, highlights, or the bold attribute — weight comes from the font name (e.g. "Matter SemiBold").
2. **Colors:** Light backgrounds (`#FFFFFF`, `#F5F5F5`, `#FEEDE6`, `#E8EFFC`) or the main gradient (title/closing only). Never `#000000` or `#141414` as a background. Text is `#141414`, never `#000000`.
3. **Footer + monogram on every content slide.** Footer left: `AI for All, from India`. Footer right: zero-padded slide number. Monogram top-right. All already present in template layouts — don't remove them.
4. **Every content slide has a visual** — image, chart, icon, or a shape from `assets/shapes/`. No text-only content slides.
5. **Every visual must be accompanied by supporting data or explanatory text** — no standalone diagrams, infographics, or charts without numbers, labels, or a written explanation alongside them on the same slide.
6. **Preserve the deck's theme** (Orange or Blue). Don't flip themes unless the user asks.
7. **Pink slides never appear in output.** They're template section markers only.

Full brand spec (all hex codes, logo variants, font weight table, XML examples): [`brand-spec.md`](brand-spec.md) — load only when needed.

# Embedded reference: brand-spec

# Brand Spec (Quick Reference)

Load this file only when you need exact hex codes, font specs, or logo rules.

## Fonts

**Display: Season Mix** — headings and captions only. Regular weight only.

**Sans-Serif: Matter** — body text, sub headings, eyebrow tags, labels, UI. Weights: Thin, Light, Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold, Heavy, Black. Plus Matter SemiMono for code/data.

### Font Size Table (Figma px → PPTX pt)

| Element | Font | Figma (px) | PPTX (pt) | XML sz |
|---------|------|------------|-----------|--------|
| Cover / hero title | Season Mix | 64px | 48pt | 4800 |
| Slide title | Season Mix | 48px | 36pt | 3600 |
| Section title | Season Mix | 36px | 27pt | 2700 |
| H2 small | Season Mix | 32px | 24pt | 2400 |
| Sub heading | Matter | 28px | 21pt | 2100 |
| Eyebrow tag | Matter | 24px | 12pt | 1200 |
| Body large | Matter | 18px | 13.5pt | 1350 |
| Footer text | Matter | 16px | 8pt | 800 |
| Body medium | Matter | 15px | 11.25pt | 1125 |
| Body small | Matter/SemiMono | 14px | 10.5pt | 1050 |
| Body x-small | Matter | 12px | 9pt | 900 |

Weight comes from font-name selection (e.g. "Matter SemiBold"), never the bold attribute. No italics, underlines, strikethrough, or highlights.

## Color Rules

- Default theme is Orange — `#A5460F` / `#FEEDE6` / `#E6651B`
- Content slides: `#FFFFFF` or `#F5F5F5` background, `#141414` text
- Title and conclusion slides: Main Gradient full-bleed, no decorative assets on top
- Never use black or dark charcoal as a slide background
- Never use raw `#000000` — use `#141414` for text
- Preserve existing theme intent; do not switch Orange to Blue unless asked

## Logo

| File | Color | Use |
|------|-------|-----|
| Sarvam Wordmark Black | `#131313` | Light backgrounds (most content slides) |
| Sarvam Wordmark White | `#FFFFFF` | Over dark end of Main Gradient (title/conclusion) |
| Sarvam Monogram Black | `#131313` | Light backgrounds, small spaces |
| Sarvam Monogram Black-1 | `#FFFFFF` | Over dark end of Main Gradient (title/conclusion) |

Rules: Default to wordmark unless space is limited. On content slides, monogram uses `#999999` tint. On cover/title slides, use wordmark. Never stretch, rotate, or recolor.

## Standard Layout Positions

| Element | x (px) | y (px) | w (px) | h (px) |
|---------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Eyebrow | 80 | 60 | 1335 | 24 |
| Heading 1 | 80 | 94 | 1335 | 64 |
| Sub Heading | 80 | 168 | 1335 | 33 |
| Monogram | 1783 | 60 | 57 | 56 |
| Footer Left | 80 | 1021 | — | 19 |
| Footer Right | right-aligned | 1021 | — | 19 |
| Content (w/ sub) | 80 | 224 | 1760 | 782 |
| Content (no sub) | 80 | 184 | 1760 | 822 |

Margins: 80px sides, 60px top, 40px bottom. Gaps: eyebrow to heading 10px, heading to sub 10px, header to content 24px, content to footer 15px.

### Multi-line heading (collision prevention)

The default positions assume a single-line heading. When a heading wraps to two lines, the subheading and content zone must shift down to avoid collision.

| Element | y (1-line) | y (2-line) |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| Heading | 94 | 94 |
| Subheading | 168 | 220 |
| Content (w/ sub) | 224 | 276 |
| Content (no sub) | 184 | 232 |

At 36pt Season Mix in a 1335px-wide box, roughly 42 characters fit on one line. If the heading exceeds this, use the two-line column. When in doubt, use the two-line positions. A small extra gap on a one-line heading is better than a collision on a two-line heading.

Preferred fix: shorten the headline so it fits one line. Only use two-line positions when the assertion cannot be shortened without losing meaning.
